journey.title: Open the filters drawer and apply a filter with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: The drawer is opened via show() instead of showModal(), which does not move focus into the dialog. This occurs because _getShowOptions returns modal:false due to a misconfiguration (e.g., backdrop false). The immediate issue is that focus remains on the trigger element after opening the drawer, preventing keyboard users from interacting with the filter controls.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify DialogBase._showElement to move focus to the first focusable element (or autofocus element) after showing the dialog, ensuring keyboard users can immediately interact with the dialog's controls.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the drawer opens, focus will be moved to the close button (or first focusable control), allowing users to tab to the In stock checkbox and activate the Show results button without needing a mouse.
functional_risks: Changing focus behavior could interfere with pages that rely on focus remaining on the trigger element after opening a dialog.
If the dialog contains no focusable elements, the fallback focuses the dialog itself (made focusable via script) or the button, which may cause unexpected focus movement.
The focus adjustment runs for both modal and non-modal dialogs, which may alter existing behavior for non‑modal dialogs that intentionally do not move focus.
verification_requirements: After activating the Filters button with Enter, focus should be on the close button (#filters-close).
Pressing Tab should move focus to the In stock checkbox (#in-stock).
Pressing Space should toggle the checkbox.
Pressing Tab twice should move focus to the Show results button (#apply).
Pressing Enter on Show results should update the applied filter text and close the drawer.
Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters button.

plan.root_cause: The drawer opens via show()/showModal() but focus remains on the trigger button (or body) instead of moving into the dialog. The native <dialog> element does not automatically focus its first focusable child when shown via showModal() in this environment. The previous synchronous focus attempt in _showElement may execute before the dialog is fully ready to receive focus.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify DialogBase._showElement to defer focus management to a microtask after the dialog is shown, ensuring the dialog and its children are fully rendered and focusable before attempting to move focus. This preserves the existing show/showModal logic while adding robust focus initialization for keyboard users.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the Filters drawer opens, focus will reliably move to the close button (#filters-close) after a microtask, allowing keyboard users to immediately Tab to the In stock checkbox, toggle it with Space, Tab to Show results, and press Enter to apply filters — all without a mouse.
functional_risks: Microtask focus may race with other microtasks in consumer code, but focus() is idempotent and safe.
If the dialog contains no focusable elements, focus falls back to the dialog element itself (which may need tabindex=-1 to be focusable).
Non-modal dialogs (show()) will also receive focus management, which may alter existing behavior for non-modal dialogs that intentionally do not move focus.
verification_requirements: After activating the Filters button with Enter, focus should be on the close button (#filters-close).
Pressing Tab should move focus to the In stock checkbox (#in-stock).
Pressing Space should toggle the checkbox.
Pressing Tab twice should move focus to the Show results button (#apply).
Pressing Enter on Show results should update the applied filter text and close the drawer.
Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters button.

plan.root_cause: The drawer opens via showModal() but no element in the dialog has the autofocus attribute, so the browser does not automatically move focus into the dialog, leaving focus on the trigger button (or body).
plan.repair_strategy: Add the autofocus attribute to the close button (#filters-close) so the browser automatically focuses it when the dialog is shown modally.

edits.after: <button type="button" class="btn-close" id="filters-close" data-bs-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close" autofocus></button>

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the Filters drawer opens, the close button receives focus automatically, allowing keyboard users to immediately Tab to the In stock checkbox, toggle it with Space, Tab to Show results, and press Enter to apply filters — all without a mouse.
functional_risks: If the drawer is ever shown non-modally (via show() instead of showModal()), the autofocus attribute will be ignored, but the drawer defaults to modal.
Only one autofocus per dialog is honored; if another element mistakenly receives autofocus, the close button would not be focused.

Pressing Space should toggle the checkbox.

Pressing Enter on Show results should update the applied filter text and close the drawer.
Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters button.
